Transformers Protectobot Action Figure (2-Pack) At first, I thought the age range on this toy was a bit too low. Then after my children gave these up and Dad got on the job, I realized quickly that the toys were just not that great.

Hot Spot is a fire truck with a really long crane on his hand that you're not supposed to be able to take off, making him awkward to pose as a robot. Once you get him into robot mode, which is no easy feat, you'll have a heck of a time getting him back into firetruck mode. Even once he's there, you can clearly see his robot hands on the top of the truck, and his legs (which form the bottom of the truck and include the back wheels), will consistently half-transform while trying to wheel him around on the ground.

All this and Hotspot is the better half of the duo. Blades, the helicopter, looks like an awkward chicken when transformed into robot mode, which is not helped by the fact that he appears to not have any hands or arms. The instructions for transforming him were incredibly difficult to decipher, as they have frequent close ups of pieces which I can't really find on my model and curvy arrows pointing at different spots. If a 31 year old with a master's degree can't figure him out, how do we expect a 6-year-old with limited patience to do it?

Rio Grande Games - Dominion: First Edition Ok, I have to start this review off by saying I had my reservations about this game. I absolutely love Euro strategy games like Puerto Rico, Agricola, Power Grid, Caylus, etc, but I'm not into card games. In fact, I pretty much hate card games.

This game was getting a lot of publicity on BoardGameGeek and everyone was raving about it so I decided that I should buy it to give it a shot. I'm glad I did.

The whole point of the game is to build your deck of cards and build up a collection of victory points. The reason this game shines is because it is a quick game that only takes about 30-40 minutes to play. It is also very fun because as you are building your deck of cards you aren't usually getting rid of the cards. If you spend some gold to buy a card that gold goes back into your discard pile and will eventually be shuffled for you to use again in another turn.

There are over 500 cards in this game with around 25 different action cards available so you can vary the game a lot depending on what cards are currently on the table. The only downside is that someone that has played the game a lot and knows a base strategy can usually beat a new player easily.

Overall this game is very addicting and short, which is a good thing. You can play multiple rounds of this game in an evening as opposed to one game of another typical Euro.
text_fidelity_b: Rio Grande Games - Dominion: First Edition

Mountains Out of Molehills | Family Board Game for 2-4 Players | Two-Level Gameboard Featuring Unique Gameplay & Custom Artwork | Great Gateway Game for Ages 9+ This is a good programmable movement game for 2 - 4 players. You draft a set of movement cards, then organize them into a plan of action for your turn, and you let your mole loose on the dirt. Everywhere you pass, you add to the pile of dirt until your dirt piles get so large that they topple over, which usually happens near the end of every game...

...but the real fun of this game is the rock. If your mole hits the rock, which moves around each round at the whim of the player who drafts the right card, then you bump, switch directions, and watch your plan fail and falter. It's funny, even for the person who gets messed up because of it.

So this is a very fun game that is light and easy to learn. I wish the underground was a little clearer in terms of where the spaces are, or that the moles were a little bit better sized for the pieces. It works though.

Educational Insights Design & Drill Bolt Buddies Recycling Truck Toy, Take Apart Toy with Electric Drill Toy, STEM Toy, Gift for Boys & Girls, Ages 3+ The quality is great, and the concept is very creative. We play with this everyday, and think it’s fun, but there’s some thoughts I want to share:

-The clear bolts are somewhat difficult to find on the carpet. I wish the ends (tips) were colored to help make them stand out since they blend into the floor and surfaces.

-The drill bit is always falling out, and it’s also clear, so it can be hard to find it when it falls, and it’s cumbersome to have to keep putting it back in the drill repeatedly.

-The drill has two directions to tighten and loosen the bolts, which is adjusted with the sliding control. The drill itself works very well at tightening and loosening, but it gets a little involved helping my child make adjustments on the drill. My child wants to tighten and loosen a single bolt at a time before moving onto the next bolt, so we’re constantly flip-flopping the controls. Maybe slightly older preschoolers would be more independent using the drill, but I think a manual tool (like a screwdriver) would be the easiest to operate.

Our favorite part of this whole set is dropping all of the bolts in the back of the truck and then opening the hatch to watch all of them tumble out. My child thinks this is hilarious and is by far the best part!

In short, I think this whole set is a great concept, but is slightly overcomplicated. I really feel a simple screwdriver would help simplify the need to shift around buttons constantly, and would even help with dexterity and motor skills more than the cumbersome drill.
text_fidelity_b: Educational Insights Design & Drill Bolt Buddies Recycling Truck Toy, Take Apart Toy with Electric Drill Toy, STEM Toy, Gift for Boys & Girls, Ages 3+

text_fidelity_a:
Repos JUST01 Just One, Various There are a lot of "just one word clues" games out there, from Codenames and Decrypto to games like Funglish, Crosstalk or Word Slam, and this game is yet another to add to that group. I think, however, that it's my secnd favorite of the bunch, and if you need a Codenames Killer, this might be up your alley.

In this team game, one player is attempting to guess a word that the rest of their team knows. Each team member writes down one word only, then compares to see if any matches are detected. If they are, those cards are discarded, and the guesser is left with fewer clues. Therefore, the more obtuse clues you get, the more you'll have, but it can be more difficult to deduce the word than if you're given a few obvious clues.

What I like about this game is that it manages to be a louder than usual team game with secrets. In Codenames or Crosstalk, two previous iterations of the concept, games are fun, but often it's players staring at the board in silence. In this one, you still can't say much, but it does lend itself to quicker play, and it's easier to communicate more freely once you have your clues written since your work is done, and the stress of the round is over for the clue-givers. This is a hard game, and it's definitely a word game, but lends itself to being an excellent family gathering game.
text_fidelity_b: Repos JUST01 Just One, Various

text_fidelity_a:
BOOMco. Rapid Madness Blaster (Discontinued by manufacturer) I'm just combining my thoughts on the various guns and products into one review, in case anyone would like to do a bit of comparing in one spot.

Darts:

The darts are kind of like a third of a straw, with a cool rubber-like tip. These tips ONLY stick to the special targets, which are on the shields(both the wearable ones and the ones that attach to the guns). There are also targets that stick to the wall. (I just taped the top of these targets, as opposed to sticking the whole thing on the wall.) We tested these out on mirrors and windows. They really don't stick to anything, but the special targets.

They're mostly bright colored, which makes it easier to find them once they've been shot. You'll have to take several time outs just to gather darts.

This company has made it perfectly clear that these darts are NOT made for little ones. I just want to reinforce that. I have an 18 month old that puts things in his mouth constantly. We found a large rock in his poo diaper. :S These are simply irresistible to him with their chewy rubber tip. He's chewed the tops off a few of them, even when we were trying to keep a close eye on him. The tops DO come off when chewed on, so these are definitely a choking hazard for little ones.

I try to teach our boys to never aim a gun at anyone, but I've been hit with a few of the darts. One hurt, but the others didn't. I think it depends on how close the gun is, and simply how the dart hits a person. In general, they don't seem to hurt too much.

Other than chewing, they seem pretty sturdy, though. They're had lots of use and bending, but they still work in the guns.

Farshot Blaster:

This is the smallest gun in this line(that we have...there seems to be a smaller "clipfire"). You pull back the top to "pump it up". It will only hold 1 dart at a time for shooting, but 2 spares fit in the bottom of the gun.

This gun is the easiest to aim, as far as target practice, and if that's what you'd like it for, I'd recommend this one. I've found it to be a great stress reliever. When the little ones are creating chaos, I can pull out this gun, tape a target to the wall, and do a little target practice.

Twisted Spinner Blaster:

This is the medium sized gun in this line. To shoot it, you pull an arm on the gun back towards yourself. The darts are loaded in the round end. It will hold 8 darts. As with all the guns, it comes with removable shields.

This one is a little harder to aim, but it's still fun.

Rapid Madness Blaster:

This is the largest gun in this line. You push and pull an arm to pump it up. The trigger is super sensitive, so it takes a couple of seconds to shoot all 20 darts that it holds. Those darts are held in a clip that slides into the side of the gun. This one is the most fun, BUT you don't get much shooting time before having to round up darts.

Bandolier:

This is an adjustable strap that you can wear across your body. It has a special target that the darts will stick to. It will also hold 12 extra darts.

Eye goggles:

These are pretty cool. As advertised, they won't fog up. They're made of a thick-like plastic/rubber, and give you "bug vision". They're also adjustable. My little ones are younger than the recommended age, but the clip kept coming off with them, and we put the goggles back together so much that I wanted to throw them away. Still, I don't think adults will have that problem, and they really are pretty cool!

Targets:

These are a little smaller than I prefer, but they do come in slightly different sizes and shapes. You get different points for different areas. The darts DO stick really well to these targets, and ONLY these targets, but if the dart hits wrong, it still won't stick. I'd say our darts stuck about half the time with the larger guns, and about 3/4th of the time with the farshot blaster. You can peel the back off and it will stick to the wall/door, but as I mentioned above, I just taped it instead. They're a fun way to create a little "battle" zone in one's room, or just simple target practice.

Overall, we've had tons of fun with these guns, and just think they're all pretty awesome.
text_fidelity_b: BOOMco. Rapid Madness Blaster (Discontinued by manufacturer)

The Schleich is well made and better than many toy dinosaurs out there, but when compared side-by-side you can really see the difference between the two. Also, I realize we probably have no way of knowing the actual color of the dinosaurs but the red on this one makes it seem a little bit cartoonish.

This dinosaur will be great for kids that play with them regularly. They will love how realistic they look. However, if you're a collector and just want these for display, I'd suggest the Papo brand instead.

Elmo is detached from the rest of the set, and he holds onto a hand "lens". Letters are hidden throughout the building, on both sides. You can tell where a letter is going to be...circle with squiggly lines. You can't tell what letter it is until Elmo's "lens" is held over it, though. To find some of the letters, the child will have to turn a couple of wheels, and lift the trash can lid, but most of them are in plain view.

This is a fun little toy for learning letters. It doesn't take up a ton of room, either. I think most children will tire quickly of it if they have full access to it, unless they have other Sesame Street toys(or something else similar) that could be used with it, apart from just hunting for letters. So I read the instructions and got the HS340 working  (hoovering) without too much hassle. I tried using the cell phone and camera portion but that would not work so I just settled with the remote control by itself. This worked fine so I began trying to learn to steer I kept it very basic, no tricks or anything that a kid might want to try indoors. After about 5 minutes of getting used to this tiny drone it hit the wall (4 feet up in the air) and slid down to the floor. I turned it off and redid the start up procedure to get more practice controlling the drone. OH NO!!! all it does now is goes side ways and immediately lunges towards the floor. I can not believe how simple it is to destroy this plastic drone. I am a very cautious adult, thus buying this HS340 so that I would have experience under my belt before using a $150 dollar HS175D ( much better than the HS175) drone. I wanted to buy my HD175D from amazon but the D version was on e-xxx  dot com website for less money (after making an offer) and better camera plus better bearings. Now I see that the return window is closed so I will simply throw this $35 (sale price) dollar paper weight in the trash. I guess I can not in good conscience recommend this drone unless you are prepared to use it only in a space that can not hit a wall at 4 foot height. So not very likely. I am quite disappointed with Holy Stone products overall.

Though this puzzle has 150 pieces… Due to the fact that all of the pieces are very unique, and some of them are even of animals, this is not the easiest puzzle to put together. Which, I think is a nice thing. Some of the pieces are very small, so this is not the type of puzzle you will want to work around small children.

At the current price of twenty-five bucks this puzzle is a bit pricier than other options. If you look around, you will certainly find other puzzles for less… But… If what you really want is a dolphin puzzle, then this is a nice one.

Bezier Games Werebeasts Ted Alspach and his Bezier Games companies bring us another small-box Werewolf themed game. This game shares a similar deception element, and artwork with previous releases, but like "Werewords", this is not a mainline Werewolf game or expansion.

In this game, players are auctioning off beasts of various types, and players are bidding on these creatures, whether they truly want them or not. This is because one major mechanic of the game is calling other players out on collecting specific types of creatures - if you are correct that they are hoarding a specific creature-type, then they are punished

Ultimately, this game did not appeal to us. It has a learning curve to playing, but once you get the hang of it, it makes the game feel a little too random. No matter what you really want, you need to either make a large number of offers, or make remarkable guesses about which goals other players have. Both are legitimate ways to win, but like a more standard "classic" board game, there is a definite strategy that you want to use, and there isn't a lot of replayability in this one for our group.

In our group, the only player who really liked it was the winner, and even she wasn't entirely sold on this one. It's fast, and simple, but it's a little too easy to make guesses on what other players want, and the artwork is strange.
text_fidelity_b: Bezier Games Werebeasts

LEGO Creator Expert 10253 Big Ben Building Kit As will become clear in this review, I am a true fan of Lego. Does that bias my review? I dont think so, you may disagree...

This is a big set. This is not a set for your younger Lego builders, not because its too hard, but because some of it will become tedious to younger minds. But us older people refusing to grow up (46 and still building with Lego!) will love this. There are several points during the build where you think "Oh WOW, thats clever" - very good.
The end result is bigger than I expected. Most of my recent large set builds have been the modular Lego City sets, which are built the right size for Lego Minifigs - this is much smaller than that! So you cannot add it to your Lego City, but you can have it in the back ground.

Its about an 8 hour build. The manual is excellent, but with less writing than some of the other ones - the Lego Eiffel Tower's Manual had a lot more information on the history of the Tower. This has a few snippets about the history, the Big Ben bell, but more would have been appreciated.

When finished, it is beautiful. You can turn the knob on the back to adjust the time - you cannot really adjust the time - the hour and minute hand are tuck, so as one turns, so does the other. But its still awesome!
The tree outside the main entrance is wonderful! one of my favorite parts of the build!

I believe that Lego is the best toy ever made. This set only re-enforces that opinion. Some Legos, when complete can be played with (the Lego City ones, for instance) but others not so much. I dont see this being played with, just built, displayed, and maybe dismantled and rebuilt.

5 stars though. A wonderful Lego set. A must have for collectors big kids, and us huge kids!
text_fidelity_b: LEGO Creator Expert 10253 Big Ben Building Kit

text_fidelity_a:
The Chameleon, Award-Winning Board Game for Families & Friends…… If you're familiar with the game Spyfall, then you're going to be able to jump right into this game. This one is quirkier, faster, but fortunately, has more replayability than Spyfall does.

In The Chameleon, each player is given a code card, or a card that says "You're the Chameleon." If you have a code card, you look up a word on a shared board, and if you're The Chameleon, you attempt to blend in with everyone else. After a little bit of finding and thinking time, each player says one word, even the Chameleon. Each player is then to attempt to argue and deduce who the Chameleon player is. Everyone votes, and that player is revealed. If it's not the Chameleon, then that player has done a good job of blending in and is the winner of the round. If it is the Chameleon, then that player gets the opportunity to guess the secret word that everyone else knew. If they get it right, they win. If not, everyone else wins.

Rounds of this game are fast, and that's a great thing. After repeat plays, it becomes fairly easy to identify the Chameleon player, but that's when the game really starts. Were you vague enough with your words so that they cannot figure out the secret code word?

There is enough replayability in this box to make the game fun for a wide range of groups, and a larger number of players. There are 40 different category clues, which means that there are 640 different possible words you could have, and that far exceeds the 20 locations of Spyfall.

Two issues prevent this from being a 5* game. The first is component quality. It's bad. Cards are awkwardly sized and flimsy, there are remainder marks on the edges of some cards from where they were cut. The second issue is that there simply aren't enough mapping location cards in the box. There's really only two possible sets of locations, and while there are no players who will be able to memorize the exact locations of words, it's possible that repeat mappings occur, and Chameleons with outstanding memories will be able to guess with regularity by reading the dice.
text_fidelity_b: The Chameleon, Award-Winning Board Game for Families & Friends……
